open_points.subject: personal-data access by agents outside the kernel
open_points.text: “Personal data — values of class `personal_data` (K-14) reach an agent only as digest and class; the owner alone reads them.” contradicts “An agent's own access to a service — as for processing a photo (decision 17) — is granted by that service and the owner outside the kernel; ... its personal-data promise (K-14) covers what the kernel itself returns.”
open_points.question: Is the prohibition on agents receiving personal-data content global, including direct service access, or limited to values returned through the kernel surface?
options: The prohibition is limited to the kernel surface; direct service policy may allow an agent to receive personal-data content.
The prohibition is global; services and the owner must never grant an agent direct access to personal-data content.
open_points.default_guess: Limit the prohibition to the kernel surface, because K-14 and the changed exclusion explicitly give it that scope.
